nodes.summary: For every element $p$ of a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and every list $xs$ over $\alpha$, the above list of the stable three-way partition of $xs$ around $p$ is the list of the elements $x$ of $xs$ with $p < x$, in their order in $xs$ and with their multiplicities.
nodes.title: The above list of a three-way partition is a filter

nodes.summary: For every element $p$ of a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and every list $xs$ over $\alpha$, the below list of the stable three-way partition of $xs$ around $p$ is the list of the elements $x$ of $xs$ with $x < p$, in their order in $xs$ and with their multiplicities.
nodes.title: The below list of a three-way partition is a filter

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an element of a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, let $xs$ be a list over $\alpha$, and let $B$, $E$ and $A$ be the below, equal and above lists of the stable three-way partition of $xs$ around $p$. Then the concatenation $B$, $E$, $A$ is a permutation of $xs$, every element $x$ of $B$ satisfies $x < p$, every element of $E$ equals $p$, and every element $x$ of $A$ satisfies $p < x$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the stable three-way partition

nodes.summary: For every element $p$ of a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and every list $xs$ over $\alpha$, the equal list of the stable three-way partition of $xs$ around $p$ is the list of the elements $x$ of $xs$ with $x = p$, in their order in $xs$ and with their multiplicities.
nodes.title: The equal list of a three-way partition is a filter

nodes.summary: For every element $p$ of a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and every list $xs$ over $\alpha$, the lengths of the below, equal and above lists of the stable three-way partition of $xs$ around $p$ add up to the length of $xs$.
nodes.title: Sizes of the three parts of a three-way partition

nodes.summary: For every element $p$ of a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and every list $xs$ over $\alpha$, the time charged by the stable three-way partition of $xs$ around $p$ equals the length of $xs$: one unit for each comparison, one comparison per element.
nodes.title: Cost of the stable three-way partition

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an element of a linearly ordered type $\alpha$. The three-way partition of a list over $\alpha$ around $p$, together with the time it is charged, is defined by recursion on the list. The empty list gives three empty lists at no cost. For a list with head $x$ and tail $xs$, one unit of time is charged for comparing $x$ with $p$, the tail $xs$ is partitioned, and $x$ is put at the front of its below list…
nodes.title: Stable three-way partition

nodes.summary: A three-way partition over a type $\alpha$ consists of three lists over $\alpha$, called below, equal and above. They are meant to hold the elements strictly below, equal to, and strictly above a pivot; the record itself imposes no condition on them.
nodes.title: Three-way partition record

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
